**Capability fit:** This is a factual/evaluative question about nutrition with a clear completion criterion — give a direct, substantive answer. Plover-235B has stronger benchmark scores across the board (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2), suggesting it'll handle the substance more reliably.

**The "don't hedge" instruction:** The user explicitly wants a direct answer without excessive qualification. Plover's higher IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3) suggests slightly better instruction-following, which is the operative demand here.

**Task-preference considerations:** The query is moderately open-ended ("evaluate how good..."). Avocet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-specified retrieval/reformatting tasks — so this sits somewhat outside its preferred zone. Plover's preferences across general task dimensions are weak/non-significant, so nothing pushes against routing it here.

None of these are huge gaps, but they all lean the same direction, so Plover was the cleaner pick. (To be clear, the actual nutritional content and any tone calibration get handled downstream — my job was just to pick the better-fitted model.)
